name: vn-en-eval-set-v4
description: VN→EN correction eval set v4 — 30 pairs targeting REGISTER errors (Step-18 taxonomy: politeness tiers, formal/casual mismatch). Each entry carries a taxonomyPatternId referencing one of the 10 patterns in src/lib/feedback/rule-packs/en-vn-register/taxonomy.ts. Zero duplicate inputs vs v1–v3.

entries.input: Respectfully and humbly, I beg to notify you that the document has been completed.
entries.expected: I would like to inform you that the document is ready.

tone.context: workplace email to manager

entries.vietlishPattern: kính trình → 'respectfully and humbly I beg to notify' — Vietnamese kính trình (formal upward report) calqued word-for-word; English business writing uses plain 'I would like to inform you'

entries.input: Dear Most Respected and Esteemed Professor, I write this letter to ask for your profound guidance.
entries.expected: Dear Professor [Name], I am writing to ask for your guidance.

tone.context: student email to professor

entries.vietlishPattern: kính gửi thầy/cô kính mến → 'Most Respected and Esteemed' — Vietnamese email salutation stacks multiple respectful modifiers; English uses a single title with no intensifiers

entries.input: Honourable Sir/Madam, accept my humble greetings and respects before I inquire about the schedule.
entries.expected: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to ask about the schedule.

tone.context: formal inquiry email

entries.vietlishPattern: kính chào + kính trọng → elaborate greeting-and-respect formula calqued; English formal openers are direct and brief — no preliminary deference passage before the question

entries.input: Hey teacher, do you have time to explain this for me?
entries.expected: Excuse me, would you have time to explain this to me?

tone.context: student addressing a teacher

entries.vietlishPattern: bạn ơi / ơi → 'hey' — Vietnamese peer-register opener 'ơi' calqued as casual 'hey'; the correct English register for a superior omits the casual opener and uses 'Excuse me'

entries.input: Boss, you can check my report today?
entries.expected: Could you please review my report today?

tone.context: employee to manager

entries.vietlishPattern: sếp, bạn có thể kiểm tra không? → direct title + casual 'you can…?' — peer-register yes/no question applied to a superior; English raises 'can' to 'could' and adds 'please'

entries.input: Hi doctor, is my health OK? You think I need medicine?
entries.expected: Hello, Doctor. Is my health all right? Do you think I need medication?

tone.context: patient consulting a doctor

entries.vietlishPattern: bạn nghĩ → 'you think?' — peer-register tag question directed at a doctor; register mismatch from applying casual VN 'bạn' address ('you') to a professional without modal hedging

entries.input: The undersigned hereby requests the provision of the above-mentioned document.
entries.expected: Could I please get a copy of the document we discussed?

tone.context: internal document request

entries.vietlishPattern: kẻ dưới / tôi → 'the undersigned' — Vietnamese bureaucratic self-reference calqued; modern English requests use first-person 'I' or 'Could I…' even in formal contexts

entries.input: This person wishes to apologize for the delay in responding.
entries.expected: I apologize for my delayed response.

tone.context: formal written apology

entries.vietlishPattern: người này muốn → 'this person wishes' — formal distancing self-reference 'người này' calqued; English always uses direct first-person 'I' in written apologies

entries.input: It is this humble employee who made the error and takes full responsibility.
entries.expected: I made the error and I take full responsibility.

tone.context: workplace accountability statement

entries.vietlishPattern: kẻ hèn mọn / nhân viên này → 'this humble employee' — formal Vietnamese self-deprecation calqued; English professional accountability uses plain 'I', not a third-person self-reference

entries.input: I received your email. I will fix it.
entries.expected: Thank you for your email. I will look into it right away.

tone.context: email reply to manager

entries.vietlishPattern: Vâng, em đã nhận được → terse acknowledgment without opening thanks; 'ạ' softening omitted — English email to a superior requires an opening 'Thank you for…' as the minimal politeness marker

entries.input: Yes, I understand. I will submit it tomorrow.
entries.expected: Yes, I understand. I will make sure to submit it by tomorrow.

tone.context: student confirming a deadline to a teacher

entries.vietlishPattern: Vâng, em hiểu rồi → acknowledgment without commitment strengthener; 'ạ' hedging omitted — polite English confirmation adds 'make sure to' or 'certainly' to reinforce deference

entries.input: I got your message. The report is done. I send it now.
entries.expected: I received your message. The report is ready — I will send it to you right away.

tone.context: work reply to senior colleague

entries.vietlishPattern: Em đã nhận được → blunt three-sentence reply without softening transitions or tense upgrade; 'ạ' register markers have no English equivalent in the learner's output

entries.input: Please explain to me the homework again.
entries.expected: Could you please go over the homework assignment again?

tone.context: student addressing a teacher

entries.vietlishPattern: Cho tôi hiểu lại bài tập → 'please explain to me' — 'Please + imperative' is the learner's only softener; 'Could you please' is the standard English modal for requests to a superior

entries.input: Give me more time to finish this task.
entries.expected: Would it be possible to have a little more time to finish this task?

tone.context: employee requesting an extension from a manager

entries.vietlishPattern: Cho tôi thêm thời gian → bare imperative 'give me' — Vietnamese 'cho + tôi' calqued directly; English requests to superiors require modal hedging ('Would it be possible to…')

entries.input: Tell me what I should do about this problem.
entries.expected: Could you advise me on how to handle this problem?

tone.context: junior employee asking a senior for guidance

entries.vietlishPattern: Nói cho tôi biết → 'tell me' — bare imperative 'Nói' calqued; English reframes the request with a modal and a softer verb ('advise', 'let me know') when addressing a superior

entries.input: No, I cannot attend the meeting tomorrow.
entries.expected: I'm afraid I won't be able to attend the meeting tomorrow.

tone.context: declining a manager's meeting invitation

entries.vietlishPattern: Không, tôi không thể → bare 'No, I cannot' — Vietnamese softened refusal phrases 'tiếc là / e rằng' not transferred; English professional decline leads with 'I'm afraid' or 'Unfortunately'

entries.input: I don't want to join the project.
entries.expected: Thank you for the opportunity, but I would prefer not to join this project.

tone.context: declining a project offer from a senior colleague

entries.vietlishPattern: Tôi không muốn → blunt 'I don't want to' — bare Vietnamese refusal 'không muốn' calqued; English declines a superior's offer with a thank-you and a hedged negative ('I would prefer not to')

entries.input: I cannot do this. Too much work.
entries.expected: I'm sorry, but I have too much on my plate at the moment and I wouldn't be able to take this on.

tone.context: declining an additional task from a manager

entries.vietlishPattern: Không được. Quá nhiều việc → fragmented blunt refusal — Vietnamese spoken brevity calqued; English professional register requires a complete, apologetic explanation with a softener

entries.input: Thanks for your help, teacher.
entries.expected: Thank you very much for your help.

tone.context: student thanking a teacher after class

entries.vietlishPattern: Cảm ơn bạn / cô → 'Thanks' (shortened) — peer-register abbreviated form; thanking a teacher in English requires 'Thank you very much' rather than the casual 'Thanks'

entries.input: Thank you, bye.
entries.expected: Thank you very much. Have a good day.

tone.context: ending a conversation with a teacher or senior

entries.vietlishPattern: Cảm ơn nhé / cảm ơn rồi tạm biệt → abrupt combined thanks-farewell — Vietnamese casual peer closing calqued; English formal register separates thanks and farewell, expands 'thank you' to 'thank you very much'

entries.input: OK thanks. I will check it.
entries.expected: Thank you. I will review it.

tone.context: email reply to a manager

entries.vietlishPattern: OK cảm ơn → informal 'OK thanks' — peer-register casual opener 'OK' combined with shortened 'thanks'; business email to a superior omits 'OK' and uses 'Thank you' as a standalone opener with a more formal verb ('review' not 'check')

entries.input: Sorry for the late reply.
entries.expected: I apologize for my late reply.

tone.context: formal email reply to a manager

entries.vietlishPattern: Xin lỗi bạn vì trả lời muộn → 'sorry' (informal) — casual 'Xin lỗi' calqued; formal English email to a superior uses 'I apologize for' or 'Please accept my apologies for'

entries.input: My bad, I forgot the deadline.
entries.expected: I sincerely apologize for missing the deadline.

tone.context: professional apology to a manager

entries.vietlishPattern: Lỗi của tôi / xin lỗi → 'my bad' — colloquial spoken apology transferred without register adjustment; professional English requires 'I sincerely apologize' when addressing a superior

entries.input: Oh sorry, I misunderstood what you said.
entries.expected: I apologize for the misunderstanding.

tone.context: apologizing to a senior colleague for a miscommunication

entries.vietlishPattern: Ồ xin lỗi → 'Oh sorry' — casual spoken VN apology with interjection calqued; English professional register drops 'Oh' and uses 'I apologize for' — attributing the misunderstanding to yourself rather than the other speaker

entries.input: Can you send me the file?
entries.expected: Could you please send me the file?

tone.context: colleague requesting a file from a senior

entries.vietlishPattern: Bạn có thể gửi file cho tôi không? → 'can you' — direct modal calqued from 'có thể'; 'could' + 'please' is the polite English form for a workplace request to someone senior

entries.input: I need you to help me with this presentation.
entries.expected: I was hoping you might be able to help me with this presentation.

tone.context: junior employee asking a senior for help

entries.vietlishPattern: Tôi cần bạn giúp → 'I need you to' — Vietnamese 'cần + person + giúp' calqued directly; English softens a favour request with 'I was hoping you might…' or 'Would you mind…'

entries.input: Can you look at my essay and give me feedback?
entries.expected: Would you be able to look at my essay and give me some feedback?

tone.context: student requesting feedback from a teacher

entries.vietlishPattern: Bạn có thể xem bài và cho tôi phản hồi không? → 'can you' without 'please' or 'would' — direct modal question without politeness upgrade; English academic favour requests raise 'can' to 'would be able to'

entries.input: Wait for me a moment, I will bring the document.
entries.expected: Please give me a moment — I will bring the document right away.

tone.context: junior employee asking a superior to wait briefly

entries.vietlishPattern: Đợi tôi một chút → 'wait for me' — bare imperative to a superior; Vietnamese spoken 'đợi tôi' calqued; English requires 'please' or a softened frame ('Could you give me a moment…') when asking a superior to wait

entries.input: Read this first, then give me your opinion.
entries.expected: Could you please read this and let me know your thoughts?

tone.context: junior employee directing a senior colleague

entries.vietlishPattern: Đọc cái này trước rồi cho tôi biết ý kiến → sequential bare imperatives 'read… give' — VN spoken instruction calqued; English reframes a request to a superior as a modal question

entries.input: Sign here and return it to me by Friday.
entries.expected: Could you please sign here and return it to me by Friday?

tone.context: junior employee directing a manager to sign a document

entries.vietlishPattern: Ký vào đây và trả lại cho tôi → bare sequential imperatives 'sign… return' — Vietnamese instruction style calqued; English wraps the entire request in 'Could you please' when the recipient is a superior
